security_audit.summary: All 15 static findings are benign documentation examples or scanner misclassifications. However, the playbook includes a user lookup without object-level authorization and a permissive CORS configuration. These template flaws require correction before production use.

remediation.issue: The user lookup endpoint returns records by identifier without checking whether the caller may access them.
remediation.suggestion: Enforce ownership or role-based authorization before loading and returning another user's record.

remediation.issue: The CORS example allows every origin, method, and header while enabling credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Use an environment-specific origin allowlist and restrict methods, headers, and credentials to application requirements.

semantic_findings.description: The user lookup requires authentication but returns any record selected by user_id without an ownership or role check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint receives current_user but never uses it before returning the requested user. Adjacent update and delete endpoints explicitly enforce ownership.

content.value_statement: New FastAPI services often mix routing, data access, and business logic. This skill provides layered patterns for async APIs, authentication, persistence, and tests.
actual_capabilities: Proposes a layered FastAPI project structure for routes, configuration, models, schemas, services, and repositories.
Demonstrates async SQLAlchemy session management and generic repository operations.
Shows dependency-injected endpoints with validation and HTTP error responses.
Provides password hashing, JWT creation, and authenticated-user dependency patterns.
Outlines pytest fixtures for isolated async database and API tests.
Identifies common async, session, typing, coupling, and testing mistakes.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and snippets, not a complete executable project generator.
Examples require dependency versions, migrations, schemas, and deployment settings from the target project.
Security-sensitive examples need review, especially authorization and CORS configuration.
The included tests cover one creation flow and do not form a comprehensive test suite.

use_cases.title: Start a Backend Service
use_cases.description: Define a maintainable package structure and async request flow for a new FastAPI service.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Architecture
use_cases.description: Separate routes, services, repositories, schemas, and configuration across a shared Python API.

use_cases.title: Teach Async API Patterns

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a FastAPI project structure for [service], including routes, schemas, services, repositories, configuration, and tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a new API with clear module boundaries

prompt_templates.title: Add Async Persistence
prompt_templates.prompt: Add async SQLAlchemy persistence for [entity], with session dependencies, repository methods, validation schemas, and rollback behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Connecting a service to an async relational database

prompt_templates.title: Implement Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Design JWT authentication for [application], including password hashing, token validation, ownership checks, configuration, and failure responses.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this FastAPI architecture for async correctness, authorization, CORS, session handling, error consistency, test coverage, and deployment risks: [details].
prompt_templates.scenario: Auditing an advanced service before deployment

output_examples.input: Plan an inventory API with products and warehouses.
output: A module map separating inventory routes, schemas, services, and repositories.
Async session dependencies with transaction and rollback behavior.
Product and warehouse endpoint responsibilities with validation boundaries.
Focused repository, service, and API test scenarios.

output_examples.input: Add secure profile update and deletion flows.
output: Authenticated endpoints with explicit owner or administrator authorization.
Service methods for validated updates and deletion outcomes.
Consistent forbidden, missing-record, and validation responses.
Tests for owners, unrelated users, administrators, and invalid tokens.

output_examples.input: Review an async FastAPI project before deployment.
output: A prioritized review of blocking calls, session lifecycle, and transaction handling.
Checks for CORS restrictions, secret management, token validation, and object authorization.
Recommended integration tests for startup, database failures, authentication, and permissions.

best_practices: Keep route handlers small and place business rules in services.
Use async-compatible clients and database drivers throughout each request path.
Test authorization, transaction rollback, validation, and error responses independently.
anti_patterns: Do not copy wildcard CORS settings into a production service.
Do not treat authentication as authorization for user-selected resources.
Do not mix synchronous database operations into async route handlers.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete FastAPI repository?
faq.answer: No. It supplies architecture guidance and connected snippets that require project-specific implementation.

faq.question: Which database style does it demonstrate?
faq.answer: It demonstrates async SQLAlchemy sessions and mentions PostgreSQL and MongoDB as possible targets.

faq.question: Does it include authentication guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers password hashing, JWT signing and validation, and authenticated-user dependencies.

faq.question: Can I use the CORS example in production?
faq.answer: No. Replace wildcard settings with an explicit allowlist and minimum required methods, headers, and credential behavior.

faq.question: What testing support is included?
faq.answer: It shows async pytest fixtures, dependency overrides, an in-memory database, and one API creation test.
